# Molecules, Avogadro's hypothesis and chemical formulae (`molecules_mole_concept`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/chemistry.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Chemistry (`chemistry`)
- Deps: needs atomic_theory, gas_laws
- Core idea: Equal volumes of ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of particles. Since two volumes of hydrogen and one of oxygen give two volumes of steam, the particles of these gases must be pairs of atoms (H2, O2) and water is H2O. Gas densities give relative molecular masses; composition across several compounds helps infer atomic masses. A mole counts exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ specified particles. Two moles of hydrogen molecules react with one mole of oxygen molecules.
- Pitfalls:
  - Writing water as HO and oxygen's weight as 8, the confusion that lasted fifty years.
  - Assuming the gaseous elements are single atoms.
  - Mixing up atoms and molecules, or weight ratios and volume ratios.
- History: europe: 1808 – Gay-Lussac, gases combine in simple volume ratios; 1811 Avogadro's hypothesis, ignored for decades; 1858–1860 Cannizzaro's Sunto and the Karlsruhe congress win acceptance; 1865 Loschmidt estimates the size of molecules
- Read:
  - Stanislao Cannizzaro, Sunto di un corso di filosofia chimica (1858)
  - Alan J. Rocke, Chemical Atomism in the Nineteenth Century: From Dalton to Cannizzaro (1984)
